title: Trained recurrent neural networks develop phase-locked limit cycles in a working memory task
relevance: Periodic input supports distinct, locally stable phase-coded memory cycles in trained rank-two rate RNNs. Poincare maps and Floquet multipliers diagnose memory-dependent cycle stability.
novelty_threat: Direct anticipation of periodic recurrent working-memory analysis; a counterexample to universal forgetting under contraction.
evidence_locator: Results: Phase-coded memories reside in stable limit cycles; Fig. 3A-C. Methods: Dimensionality and dynamics of low-rank RNNs with periodic input; Poincare maps and linear stability analysis, Eq. (9) and variational equation.
limitations: Two categorical memories; continuous-time low-rank tanh model, specialized oscillatory output. Not a matched higher-order repetition comparison.

title: Transitions in echo index and dependence on input repetitions
relevance: Theorems connect minimum symbol-block repetition lengths to attractor multiplicity; long blocks can produce a unique response under a uniform single-attractor assumption.
novelty_threat: Direct theoretical anticipation of repetition-dependent loss or preservation of initial-state distinctions.
evidence_locator: Assumption 2.1; Lemma 2.2; Theorems 2.3 and 2.4, printed p. 9; Section 2.3/Fig. 3 obstruction example; Sections 3.1-3.3 leaky-tanh examples.
limitations: Compact-state switched maps and hyperbolic-attractor assumptions; symbol run length differs from the plan's whole-motif repetition with matched run lengths. Journal DOI not verified.

title: The Echo Index and multistability in input-driven recurrent neural networks
relevance: Defines input-dependent multiplicity of stable recurrent responses and explains reliable computation beyond global echo-state uniqueness.
novelty_threat: Multiple retained memories under a common driver are an established phenomenon, not a new exception discovered by this project.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract and related DOI metadata, version 2.
limitations: Full theorem assumptions and numerical protocols not audited here.

title: Echo State Property Linked to an Input: Exploring a Fundamental Characteristic of Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance: Input-specific ESP distinguishes dependence on input history from arbitrary initial conditions. Uniform shrinking bounds imply uniqueness; a periodic driver with ESP has a response whose period divides the input period.
novelty_threat: The proposed unique forced response and history-washout foundations are standard input-dependent synchronization theory.
evidence_locator: Definition 2.2, author-PDF p. 5; Lemma 2.2, pp. 7-8; Proposition 2.3 and proof, p. 9; Section 2.1 cautions on folklore.
limitations: Compact state space and entire-solution definitions. Contraction bound is sufficient; negative local exponents alone do not establish global uniqueness. First name expanded using university author record.

title: The echo state approach to analysing and training recurrent neural networks - with an Erratum note
venue: GMD Report 148; corrected author version dated 2010
relevance: Introduces echo states as functions of left-infinite input history and readout training; includes periodic generators and multiple-switch examples.
novelty_threat: Initial-state forgetting while retaining input-history information is foundational, so these must not be conflated.
evidence_locator: Corrected PDF title page/erratum notice; Introduction and Definition 1, pp. 3-5.
limitations: 2010 author version corrects a flaw in Definition 3 and Proposition 1 of the 2001 report. Original theorem equivalences were not independently audited.

title: Short term memory in echo state networks
relevance: Foundational short-term-memory capacity reference for reconstruction of past inputs from recurrent states.
novelty_threat: A memory-capacity versus state-dimension statement needs this antecedent and its task/readout assumptions.
evidence_locator: Author-uploaded report title page: May 28, 2002; footnote: GMD Report 152, publication March 28, 2002. Author publication index labels the item 2001.
limitations: Year conflict in author index retained explicitly; 2002 follows report title-page publication note. Capacity theorem not read in this audit; Fraunhofer PDF endpoint timed out.

title: Stimulus-dependent suppression of chaos in recurrent neural networks
relevance: Mean-field theory links oscillatory drive amplitude and frequency to suppression of chaotic fluctuations and phase locking.
novelty_threat: Input-induced stabilization and frequency-selective chaos suppression precede a generic Floquet-collapse claim.
evidence_locator: Abstract; bibliographic header; Eq. (1)-(3) and Fig. 1 inspected to verify model/driver definition.
limitations: Random continuous-time rate circuits; no required-history recall endpoint. Deep mean-field derivation not reviewed. Abbott's expanded first name verified from Columbia.

title: Short-Term Memory in Orthogonal Neural Networks
relevance: Studies retrieval of temporal sequences from the instantaneous state in linear discrete networks; orthogonal and distributed shift-register capacity scales with size.
novelty_threat: Preservation controls and claims connecting effective dimension to memory must compare established orthogonal-memory results.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract, journal-reference and DOI fields.
limitations: Specific linear/noise/capacity normalization assumptions not audited from full text.

title: Memory traces in dynamical systems
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 105(48): 18970-18975
relevance: Defines Fisher-memory matrices for past-input sensitivity and derives noise-whitened linear expressions. Normal versus nonnormal dynamics have different retention capabilities.
novelty_threat: The noise-resolved task-channel/Fisher sensitivity framework is established; a renamed CPG metric is not itself a theoretical contribution.
evidence_locator: Author PDF pp. 18970-18971: Fisher Memory Matrix, Eq. (1)-(5); normal-network memory curve and sum rule.
limitations: Local input sensitivity and explicitly specified dynamical noise; bounds depend on input/noise/weight normalization. Does not equate covariance rank with nonlinear global memory.

title: Information Processing Capacity of Dynamical Systems
relevance: Capacity framework decomposes reconstructable input functions with readouts of dynamical observations.
novelty_threat: Generic rank-limited reconstruction-capacity claims have direct antecedents; target basis and readout class must be specified.
evidence_locator: Publisher/search abstract and article metadata; primary full-text access attempts recorded in theory-review.md.
limitations: No theorem promoted from search snippets. Nature redirect and Europe PMC access failed; full theorem hypotheses need a later verified reading.

title: Linking connectivity, dynamics and computations in low-rank recurrent neural networks
relevance: Relates structured low-rank connectivity to low-dimensional computations in recurrent networks.
novelty_threat: Low dimension is often a computational solution; the project must show loss of required information rather than treating low rank as damage.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract and journal metadata.
limitations: Connectivity rank, activity dimensionality and task-channel rank are different quantities; full derivations not audited.

title: Dynamics of random recurrent networks with correlated low-rank structure
relevance: Connects correlations between random and low-rank connectivity to dynamical regimes and spectral outliers.
novelty_threat: Structured low-dimensional dynamical mechanisms have mature analytic antecedents.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract; published author-PDF title/DOI metadata.
limitations: Autonomous/random structured networks are not equivalent to trained periodic full-state Jacobian products.

title: Lyapunov spectra of chaotic recurrent neural networks
relevance: Analyzes full Lyapunov spectra of recurrent dynamics and effects of input fluctuations on chaotic entropy and attractor dimension.
novelty_threat: Reduced dynamical dimension with forcing is established; connecting it to required-task memory must add evidence.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract, journal reference, DOI; MPI publication metadata.
limitations: 2020 preprint versus 2023 journal year distinguished. Attractor dimension is not covariance PR or target decodability.

title: On Lyapunov Exponents for RNNs: Understanding Information Propagation Using Dynamical Systems Tools
relevance: Uses Lyapunov analysis to study propagation and performance in recurrent networks.
novelty_threat: Applying conditional exponents to learned RNNs is established methodology rather than sufficient novelty.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract and author metadata.
limitations: No claim that exponent sign proves global history forgetting; journal/workshop venue and DOI not verified here.

title: The spectrum of covariance matrices of randomly connected recurrent neuronal networks with linear dynamics
relevance: Analyzes recurrent connectivity and covariance spectral structure in linear networks.
novelty_threat: A covariance-concentration mechanism needs comparison to established random-network spectra, not just visualization.
evidence_locator: Publisher abstract, authors and citation header.
limitations: The covariance/noise model differs from finite required-history clouds; current audit does not reproduce equations.

title: How the brain keeps the eyes still
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 93(23): 13339-13344
relevance: Treats analog persistent memory as an attracting line of equilibria, explains tuned feedback and slow drift, and contrasts discrete noise-resistant point attractors.
novelty_threat: Continuous-memory neutral directions and the categorical/continuous distinction are classical foundations, not candidate novelty.
evidence_locator: Author-paper scan, pp. 13342-13343: Eq. (4)-(5), linear tuning/eigenvalue discussion, nonlinear approximation, and explicit line-versus-point-attractor contrast.
limitations: Exact manifold neutrality does not guarantee robustness to noise or mistuning. Expanded author name retains published H. initial; no unverified expansion.

title: Fundamental limits on persistent activity in networks of noisy neurons
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 109(43): 17645-17650
relevance: Bounds noise-induced diffusion of continuously stored memory using an information-diffusion relation.
novelty_threat: Neutral tangent directions alone cannot support claims of robust memory; continuous-attractor noise limits are prior theory.
evidence_locator: Abstract; Results model assumptions and Diffusive Drift due to Ongoing Neural Noise inspected.
limitations: Poisson spiking/weak-fluctuation approximation and tuned-away systematic drift; supporting derivations not deeply audited.

title: Learning dynamics in linear recurrent neural networks
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 267: 49860-49902
relevance: Derives task-dependent linear-RNN learning dynamics, stability/extrapolation effects, and a recurrent/feedforward regularization tradeoff.
novelty_threat: Training-induced memory tradeoffs and temporal precedence have close recent theoretical antecedents.
evidence_locator: Official PMLR abstract and BibTeX; full author names from proceedings.
limitations: Restricted linear learning theory; frozen-weight repetition interventions could extend it. DOI and arXiv identifier not verified.

title: Temporal superposition and feature geometry of RNNs under memory demands
relevance: Derives delayed-recall loss terms and links temporal feature geometry, interference and memory demand; nonlinear recurrence enables selective forgetting.
novelty_threat: Direct anticipation of mechanistic geometry-memory analysis, including spectral-radius changes and geometric transitions.
evidence_locator: Sections 3.1-3.4, pp. 3-5; Section 4.1 Eq. (5), p. 5; Sections 4.2-4.4, pp. 6-8; Appendices A-B and D.1-D.3, pp. 18-24.
limitations: Linear/ReLU models, independent sparse inputs and delayed recall; no matched periodic-versus-nonperiodic test. Appendix D.1 generic spectral claim has degenerate unobserved-mode exceptions; do not copy as universal ESP theorem. DOI/arXiv ID unverified.

title: How Temporal Correlations Shape Memory in Linear Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance: Under aligned linear learning assumptions, temporal covariance changes the effective cost of memory. A newest-pair ratio gives the local release boundary; strong periodicity can change the global crossing.
novelty_threat: Very close to correlation/repetition-dependent memory transitions; a new fixed-weight higher-order forcing result must separate local release from global transition.
evidence_locator: Mathematical Setup, Assumptions 1-4; Lemmas 1-2, Eq. (8)-(9); Appendix C; Appendix E, Scope condition and Table S4.
limitations: Fixed singular-vector/aligned-initialization and covariance restrictions. Lemma 2 local boundary is not universally the global optimum transition; periodicity examples explicitly qualify it.

title: Fundamental bound on the persistence and capacity of short-term memory stored as graded persistent activity
relevance: Derives recall-precision limits for continuous persistent-memory channels and considers protective encoding.
novelty_threat: Noise-aware graded-memory bounds must be positioned against this prior channel-based framework.
evidence_locator: Publisher abstract and article citation.
limitations: Model-dependent graded activity/noise assumptions; does not bound arbitrary nonlinear finite-category codes.

title: Optimal sequence memory in driven random networks
relevance: Dynamic mean-field theory connects input, Lyapunov stability and sequence memory; locally expansive but nonchaotic dynamics can improve memory.
novelty_threat: A single exponent threshold or edge-of-chaos narrative cannot replace task-specific retention measurements.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract; publisher journal reference and DOI.
limitations: Random-network mean-field regime, not a general gated-model theorem; local expansion and asymptotic stability must be distinguished.

title: Dynamics of learning to integrate in linear recurrent neural networks
relevance: Analyzes learning of long integration timescales through recurrent spectral outliers and extends to damped oscillatory filters.
novelty_threat: Learning neutral/slow or oscillatory memory modes has recent analytic treatment; the project should add inference-specific causal evidence.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract and version history (24 March 2025; 8 June 2026).
limitations: Analytically restricted linear networks; DOI/journal venue not verified. Full derivations not reviewed.

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
relevance: Computes input-conditioned equilibrium representations through repeated shared updates and implicit differentiation.
novelty_threat: Convergence of depth loops can be useful computation while input sensitivity remains; it is not automatically memory collapse.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract and author/venue metadata.
limitations: Finite-depth looped transformers with depth/position schedules and caches need separate complete-state definitions; DOI not verified.
